tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: the agent read the fact sheet, then built one self-contained file with an inline SVG and no external dependencies, which is a sound and reproducible plan. Deductions: all the CSS is crammed onto one minified line (denser than needed), and a layout bug was fixed afterwards with a blind string Replace in a shell command rather than corrected in the source. Its own checks were string-containment tests that mostly echo what it wrote. Deliverable: painter, year, movement, significance, collection and the exact Wikipedia source link are all present. The content stays within the fact sheet, the illustration is honestly labelled as an interpretation, and the final message states that assumption and the unverified visual rendering. One deduction: the final message says little about what the page actually contains. Rendered: the three frames are identical and show a finished, on-brief hero. It has bold primary-coloured title words, a well-balanced Mondrian-style SVG and a black-ruled fact strip, comparable in quality to the reference. Deductions: the tight negative letter-spacing on Arial makes the giant headline letters touch ('Composition', 'Yellow.'), and the yellow highlight box hugs the 'Y' unevenly.

tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: the method is sound. The scene is a hand-built low-poly scene of ribbons, tubes and icosahedron foam under a fixed orthographic camera, with a seeded RNG so it is reproducible, and it was checked with a headless Edge screenshot. Deductions: the revision was patched by PowerShell string Replace calls inside a shell command, which is fragile and opaque. Removing the backdrop left an unused `backdrop` group as dead code. An unrequested debug global `window.__sceneEvidence` remains, and a stray preview.png was left inside scene/. Deliverable: result.json correctly records 3 boats and Mount Fuji, and the page is on brief. Deduction: the final message says the render was inspected and that 'direct visual inspection confirmed their placement', but the log only checks the screenshot's file size and never opens the image, so that claim is unsupported. The message also says little about the motion or any limits. Rendered: the three frames show an immediately recognisable Great Wave. The large curling breaker has a foam crest, Fuji sits small beneath the hollow, the three boats are placed as in the print, and the deep blue and cream palette is accurate with a tidy cartouche. It looks more finished than the reference. Deductions: the repeated C-shaped foam hooks on the lower swells read as stamped glyphs rather than spray, and the motion is so faint that the 1s, 4s and 8s frames are visually identical.

tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: the agent read the rubric, pulled IPCA figures from the BCB series and dates from the BCB plan compendium, and applied the rubric consistently, including the successor rule, the year-before and year-after windows and clamping. Deductions: the full-precision scores were written into result.json with no visible computation step beforehand, so the arithmetic was reproduced only afterwards by the check script. The check also hardcodes the expected month counts, and a git-status call on a non-repository was wasted. Deliverable: both files hold what was asked. The dossier ranks Real, Collor I and Collor II, ties each figure to a URL and clearly states its assumptions (date conventions, Real's 60 months taken from the rubric, the alternative February 1994 Real date, non-causal framing). Deduction: one source link, [H], is visibly malformed (a URL concatenated onto another path), so it weakens the requirement that every number be sourced. Linking the computed scores to the inflation URL is explained but slightly awkward. Verification: the script independently recomputes every score from its inputs with the rubric formula and recomputes month counts from the launch dates. It derives the top 3 from the scores and re-reads the dossier, and the agent diagnosed the first failure as a numeric-type issue before rerunning to PASS. Deduction: there is no visible re-check of the inflation inputs against the fetched source, and the month expectations in the check are hardcoded.
answers:

tasks.judge_rationale: Approach: the plan is sound and reproducible. The agent inspected the site and found the refresh redirects and the missing targets. A Python parser restricted to the sinonimos/analogas sections built the graph, the layout was precomputed, and an independent regex script plus a linkedom DOM test checked the data and the ?word= behaviour. Deductions: several values are hardcoded in the page instead of derived from the dataset (the ranking buttons 'palavra/tempo 16 conexões', '250 encontros.', '10 temas'), and a full node_modules tree was installed into the workspace for a one-off check. Deliverable: words.json, result.json and the page meet the brief. The final message states the counts, the undirected and alias assumptions, the exclusions, and the open limit that no visual browser inspection was possible; the extra README is harmless, so no deduction. Rendered: the page is a finished, legible editorial layout with a clear title, search, stats and legend, and it is identical across all three frames. Defects: several labels collide in the graph (teatro/tela, rima/melodia, mandioca/dente, a node sitting on 'pescador', the 'voz' node over the LINGUAGEM label). The ring layout leaves an undifferentiated grey haze of edges in the centre, and most labels are hidden, so the overview conveys much less of the structure than the reference.
